# `kernel/GpuDeviceBroker.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/GpuDeviceBroker.js`

GpuDeviceBroker.js — per-app GPU device facades, quotas, and adapter redaction. WHY a facade and not a Proxy of the real GPUDevice? Host objects with internal slots (GPUDevice/GPUQueue) fail brand checks when a Proxy is handed back to other WebGPU APIs (notably `GPUCanvasContext .configure({ device })`). So we hand apps a *forwarding facade*: a plain object that forwards to the real device and returns real resource objects (for example GPUBuffer/GPUTexture). GPUCommandEncoder is wrapped so compute passes remain capability-gated even after a device facade is issued. The only host API that consumes the device object itself is `context.configure` — apps should get their canvas via `gpu.acquireSurface` (configured by the OS with the REAL device), so they never need to pass the facade anywhere. If an app does configure a canvas itself with the facade it fails closed (safe). POLICY: every app, including trusted built-ins, receives a facade that: - tracks + quota-checks every createBuffer / createTexture (via VRAMTracker), - counts pipelines / shader modules / queue submits per app, - enforces a command-submit budget (anti-runaway), - partitions the shader-module cache per app (no cross-app cache sharing), - fails closed after release or device loss until the broker re-issues a fresh facade. Raw GPUDevice lifetime authority is kernel-internal. Trust tier may affect information redaction and other syscalls, but never selects a raw device.

## Functions

### `captureGpuOwnerAllocationTelemetrySource(ownerAuthority)`

Capture original-mount requested-allocation accounting, not physical VRAM or Realm owner authority. Only an original openOwner lease selects a source. Release does not destroy accepted resources; observation survives release. Forgetting the ledger reports unavailable numeric fields, never cleanup. Surface and other untracked resource bytes remain explicitly unavailable.

### `captureGpuOriginalFacadeBindingSource(ownerAuthority, facade)`

Authenticate one exact original mount/facade pair without inspecting caller properties or adopting resources. Identity4 is historical broker issuance; assertCurrent() runs the retained original facade guard, not a caller check. This source grants no allocation, enumeration, destruction or Realm authority. It proves neither which facade a configured syscall will return nor the authenticity of that syscall provider. The host must check the actual return. The guard uses the broker's existing trusted publication/admission semantics; it is not isolation from direct mutation of privileged broker internals.

### `createGpuOriginalResourceAllocationCohort(ownerAuthority, facade, admit)`

Derive two restricted allocation routes from one original owner/facade pair. The required admit function is only an additional synchronous restriction: its normal return is not Realm ownership or lifecycle evidence. It receives no arguments, private records, resources or receiver authority. Each original issuance is assigned to this cohort before its destroy getter. Existing resources and ordinary facade allocations cannot be enrolled later. The frozen result is exactly identity/createBuffer/createTexture/snapshot/close. Snapshot retains the original seven-field historical issuance projection, including rejected candidates, after close or mount revocation. Close stops creation only and is not destruction. The private retention set now drains an issuance only after an observed normal original destroy return. Unresolved entries remain retained until a later observation or authorized explicit retry. A generic cohort and caller-supplied admission function prove no Realm origin.

### `createGpuOriginalCohortWorkView(originalCohort)`

Derive ordinary work from an exact original cohort's retained issuer and admission operation. This accepts no new callback or claimed Realm identity. Each result is an independent frozen WorkView8/Queue3, not an owner facade, allocation route, teardown capability or original-facade registry member. Generic cohort admission is still only an additional synchronous restriction. The approved protected standard shader profile snapshots shader descriptors. Other native argument conversions and raw resource children remain separate boundaries; this view does not silently normalize those other descriptors.

### `destroyGpuOriginalResourceAllocationCohort(originalCohort, authorize)`

Restriction-gated destruction of one exact original allocation cohort. A supplied callback only restricts this original capability; it authenticates no Realm identity or teardown root. No resource, original operation or private record is passed to it. It must synchronously throw to deny an operation. A valid call permanently seals creation. An in-flight allocation may still return an unknown candidate, so ALLOCATION_PENDING throws without a receipt; retry explicitly after that creation unwinds. Each call visits at most 256 retained candidates once. Unavailable, running and failed operations remain unresolved and rotate to the tail for fair later retries. No retry is scheduled. Counts certify observed synchronous original-destroy returns only. Device loss, mount revocation, accounting removal and unavailable operations never imply abandonment or physical GPU reclamation. Old snapshot7 remains historical.

### `captureGpuOriginalResourceOwnershipSource(ownerAuthority, facade)`

Historical original-facade/mount issuance, not Realm enrollment or terminal authority. Lookup never reflects on the supplied resource or invokes it. `returned` means an observed original synchronous call returned normally, not physical GPU reclamation, Promise settlement or outer app acceptance. Unwrapped direct destruction is deliberately unobserved. Release, recovery and forgotten accounting do not rewrite this original issuance's identity.

### `bucketLimits(limits)`

Bucket GPUSupportedLimits into a coarse, plain object. Reduces fingerprint entropy (exact limits vary per GPU/driver) while keeping values usable. Returns a plain object with the same keys apps read.

### `bucketAdapterInfo(info)`

Redact a rich adapter-info report down to a coarse, low-entropy summary for untrusted apps. Keeps the vendor *bucket* and capability booleans; drops the precise renderer string, driver version, device id, and exact limits.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
